- validate routing policies (latency vs cost), and
- run a short load profile against your baseline to estimate per-token cost under peak traffic.

- Wed Apr 14, 09:00–11:00

If none of those work, send a couple alternatives and we’ll adjust. I’ll bring Marcus (runtime lead) for the load tests and Dev (solutions engineer) for the prompt walkthrough. Karthik will join for the kickoff framing and rollout questions.

Agenda and pre-reads attached — please skim the prompt set before the session so we can jump straight into live runs.

Cheers,

Team —

Thanks for a productive session. Highlights:
- Prompt runs: we validated baseline prompt-set-v2.json and found a 7% latency degradation at 50× bursts vs 1×; Marcus’s suggested kernel selection improved median latency by ~12%.
- Routing: we liked the cost-latency routing demo; Karthik recommended a canary-to-primary fallback window of 200–300ms.
- Load tests: the short 10-min load profile matched our expected QPS; full load plan needs one more run with a longer tail.

Action items I captured:
1) Redwood: run a 60-minute extended load (Marcus) — target Thu Apr 15, owner Marcus Lin
2) Veridian: provide a 24-hour representative traffic trace (Sienna) — target Fri Apr 16
3) Joint: finalize prompt tuning doc and flag 3 prompts for production guardrails (Dev & Tom) — target Mon Apr 19
4) Redwood: share detailed cost estimates per-route (Karthik) — target Mon Apr 19

Please correct anything I missed. We’re excited to move to a 2-week pilot if the extended load looks good.

—Tom
